name: 2B Reversal

card.context: A strong stock, RS 80 or more, above its 200-day, often near the 50-day or 200-day while the whole market washes out under its own prior lows and reclaims them. The reading turning from Orange or Yellow toward Green.
card.pattern: A swing low made 5 to 60 sessions ago with a rally of at least 1 ATR off it. The first break under that low goes no more than 3% under it and fails to follow through.
card.trigger: PREV LOW RECLAIM: price trades back above the broken swing low on the break day or within the next 3 sessions, bought at market, no more than 4% above the low.
card.stop: A few cents under the lowest low of the undercut, the new extreme. On a same-day reclaim that is the day's low. More than 3% away: size down, or wait for the hourly higher low.
card.failure_mode: The reclaim does not hold: price trades back under the new low within days, usually while the market is still making lower lows. Out at once. A third of all hits never reached 1R.

criteria.statement: The close on the reclaim day is above the 200-day SMA.

options.basis: B26 as written: longs above the 200-day only (the dossier's rule)
a named exception for 2Bs below the 50-day but above the 200-day is already allowed; the question is the owner's 2025-12-07 note on undercuts below the MAs (28:9)

criteria.evidence: About half of all liquid 2B bottoms in the dossier's check (71,669 of 144,669) were below the 200-day and did no better (27.6% to 3R). One of Bracco's seven named 2Bs (GEV) was below it on the reclaim day. The curriculum's SPY 2011 example was far below it. The owner: the undercut below the MAs is not something I generally do.

criteria.statement: Best when the 200-day is rising: higher than it was 20 sessions ago.
criteria.evidence: Bracco's names put in this exact reversal pattern near their 200-day moving averages. The 20-session window is the glossary's reading of rising; the dossier says rising without a number.

criteria.statement: Best when the undercut low sits at the 50-day or 200-day SMA: within 0.25 ATR above the line or up to 1 ATR under it.

measure.what: undercut low against the 50-day or 200-day SMA

criteria.evidence: The dossier says near the 50-day or 200-day, the way Bracco describes it, with no distance. The band is the glossary's touch band, not a number from the dossier; the owner may prefer his own words.

criteria.statement: The indexes are washing out under their own prior lows and reclaiming them, and leaders undercut their lows at the same time. A market still making lower lows with no reclaim is not the place.
criteria.evidence: Bracco 2026-04-05: as the indices broke down and trended significantly below previous lows, all the RS names briefly undercut those previous lows and reclaimed as market came off the lows. Scan: NVDA 2024-04-18, AMD 2024-04-16 and TSLA 2023-08-11 were clean 2Bs in leaders that failed while the market was still falling; the dossier calls 8.7 a gate, not a footnote. In the second pass, leaders with SPY under its 50-day were higher 20 sessions later 61% of the time against 55% for a random day, but the median stop was 3.3%.

criteria.statement: Green market: full risk. Yellow: smaller and fewer. Orange: A+ only. Red: mostly cash and shorts. Start with a few positions as the reading turns Green again.
criteria.dossier_ref: 8.7 Best market conditions; 7 B18, F65, F68 row
criteria.evidence: F68: after a correction, when the reading turns Green again, start with a few positions and add more only as the first ones work. Bracco's best 2Bs come as the market makes a low and turns.

criteria.statement: RS rating 80 or more, in a strong group.

options.basis: C31 applies: RS 80 or more, as Bracco's RS names (the dossier's lean)
a 2B is a mean-reversion trade and C31 exempts it

criteria.evidence: Bracco's version is RS names. The dossier's check could not read an RS rating; its leader proxy (6-month gain of 30% or more, within 25% of the 52-week high, rising 200-day) did no better in R than the rest (26.8% against 27.1% to 3R) but pointed up more often in a market pullback. The register's default lists the washout U&R, not the 2B, in the exempt class.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day on average.
criteria.evidence: The scan used the house floor on the 50-day average. The owner wants good spots on good stocks.

criteria.statement: The position is at most 1% of average daily volume.
No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report.
criteria.evidence: AAPL 2014-10-15 and MU 2025-12-17 were clean 2Bs that worked and were dropped from the candidates because B22 forbids the buy. The ten examples were checked against the earnings table by hand.

criteria.statement: An orderly drift into the low: no outsized red news candle just before the break.
criteria.evidence: By analogy from the owner's Oops rulings: a big red candle prior takes the stock off his list (ULTA, FLEX, C, GTLB). The dossier gives no size for outsized; the Oops card measures it (no bar in the 5 sessions before with a drop over 4% or a range over 2.5 ATR), and this card can borrow that number if the owner wants one test for the family.

criteria.statement: The level is a swing low (no lower low in the 5 sessions on each side) made 5 to 60 sessions before the break, with a rally of at least 1 ATR off it before the break. Also allowed, by the owner's usage: last week's low, a range low, or the low of a pullback to the 20 EMA or 50 SMA.

measure.what: sessions from the swing low to the break day
measure.and: highest high between the swing low and the break at least 1 ATR(14) above the swing low

options.basis: any swing low 5 to 60 sessions old with a rally between (the dossier's proposal; Turtle Soup's 3 to 4 sessions and Bulkowski's median 21 days sit inside the window)
only multi-week lows the whole market can see (the A cue in the register's default)
also last week's low and range lows, as in the owner's posts (QBTS, TEAM, RDDT)

criteria.evidence: Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim): the age of the level (6 to 15 sessions against over 30) made little difference, 55.5% against 59.9% to 3R (was 42.3% against 44.1% with fills at the open). The dossier's check: 5 to 20 sessions old 27.1% against 21 to 60 sessions 26.9%. Sperandeo gives no lookback; nothing in the house sets one (the starterScans note is right).

criteria.statement: A one-day dip under yesterday's low is an Oops, not a 2B: the level must be at least 5 sessions old.
criteria.dossier_ref: 8.1 The level; 5.3 The Model Book card
criteria.evidence: The Model Book glyph shows a one-day dip under the previous candle's low in a straight decline, with no prior swing low: it reads as an Oops or Turtle Soup Plus One, not a 2B. The draft curriculum calls the Oops the gap-open variant of the identical mechanics.

criteria.statement: The break is the first session to trade under that low since it formed.

measure.what: sessions that traded under the swing low before the break day

criteria.evidence: Sperandeo's previous extreme. Chart IQ's two_b_reversal label, replayed on the same bars, fired 149,226 times and only 2.5% were the first break of the swing low; only 42.2% closed back above it. That is a bounce in a decline, not a 2B.

criteria.statement: The lowest low of the undercut is no more than 3% under the prior low (about 1 ATR or less in most leaders), so the stop fits A13. Deeper undercuts only with a smaller size or a later, tighter entry.

measure.what: (prior low - lowest low of the undercut) / prior low

options.basis: the dossier's line, from A13 (undercuts under 2% did best in R)
Bulkowski's 2B: the second extreme overshoots by up to 5% (S4)
Sperandeo gives no depth

criteria.evidence: Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim): an undercut of 1% or less (26,267 hits) reached 3R 64.7% and 5R 55.0%; 1% to 2% 48.6% / 34.8%; 2% to 3% 41.8% / 26.8% (was 44.4% / 32.6%, 41.4% / 28.7%, 38.4% / 23.9% with fills at the open). The dossier's check: over 5% reached 5R only 7.2% of the time with a median 8.96% stop. Six of UCT's seven named 2Bs undercut by 1.8% to 15.8% (HOOD 15.8%, PLTR 11.3%, RKLB 12.4%); only SPOT and NFLX stayed under 4%.

criteria.statement: A close back above the prior low on the break day or within the next 3 sessions. Same day or next day is the better grade.

measure.what: sessions from the break day to the first close back above the prior low

options.basis: same day only (Turtle Soup)
same day or next day (Turtle Soup Plus One; Sperandeo's within one day or less for a minor extreme)
within 3 sessions (the dossier; Sperandeo's three to five days for an intermediate extreme, 1993)

criteria.evidence: Sperandeo 1993: a minor 2B fails within one day or less, an intermediate one within three to five days, a major one within seven to ten days; 1994 adds immediately. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim): a same-day reclaim (28,067 hits) 64.3% / 54.2% with the stop under the day's low, which is known only at the close (a 5-minute check with the stop under the low so far gave 31.0% to 3R), a next-day reclaim (12,149 hits) 47.9% / 33.6% and 39.4% / 26.0% for 2 to 3 days (was 41.0% / 29.6% same day and 39.5% / 26.0% for 2 to 3 days, with the same-day fill at the open). The dossier's close-entry check: same-day reclaims had tighter stops (1.66% against 3.07%) and more 5R wins (18.6% against 14.8%).

criteria.statement: The reclaim day closes in the upper half of its range. A close in the bottom half invalidates it.

measure.what: (close - low) / (high - low) of the reclaim day

criteria.dossier_ref: 8.5; 9 A+ (closing in the top part of the day's range)
criteria.evidence: The house Undercut & Reclaim scanner requires the upper half. The scan used it as a gate. Example: QCOM 2020-09-21 closed in the top 6% of its range, MU 2024-02-20 in the top 4%.

criteria.statement: Quiet on the break (at or under the 50-day average volume), heavier on the reclaim. A grade booster, not a gate.

options.basis: quiet failure, heavier reversal: Sperandeo (S1); the dossier's check agrees, weakly
heavy volume on the failed break is the trapped crowd: the draft curriculum M10.L2 (S13), no source

criteria.evidence: Sperandeo: the failure usually occurs on low to normal volume. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim): a quiet break (18,364 hits) 57.7% / 46.9% against 56.6% / 43.8% for a loud one (over 1.5x) (was 43.0% / 30.8% against 42.3% / 29.3% with fills at the open). The dossier's check: break-day volume under 1.0x reached 5R 19.0%, 1.5x or more 13.9%. The ten examples broke on 0.64x to 1.10x.

criteria.statement: Price trades back above the broken swing low after the undercut. A market order when it trades back above (intraday), or near the close if the day closes back above.

measure.what: intraday price during regular hours, after the undercut

options.basis: a market order when it trades back above the old low (the dossier; E57; Sperandeo and Turtle Soup use a stop order at the level, the same price in practice)
only on a close above
the owner's AMD way: the next hourly higher low
over the reclaim day's high

criteria.evidence: Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10: the fill at the level plus a cent, or the open when a later session gapped above it): 56.7% to 3R and 45.1% to 5R (was 42.7% and 30.2%, when a same-day reclaim was filled at the day's open). The dossier's check with an entry at the reclaim day's close: 27.0%, the same as a random day. The gap between 27% and 57% is mostly the fill: a later, higher fill with the same stop makes R larger and 3R farther away. With a stop a few cents under a shallow undercut, R is often under 1% of price, so slippage matters more here than in any other setup.

criteria.statement: For a deep undercut or a stop over 3%: wait for the next hourly higher low after the reclaim, or an inside day, and buy its break with the stop under that day's low.

measure.note: then the entry moves to the hourly higher low or the inside day's break

criteria.evidence: The owner on AMD 2026-09-06: failed breakdown below $460 with strong candle, next higher low on the hourly is actionable. The dossier proposes this for the 3% condition. In the market-washout cases Bracco names, the stop beyond the undercut was a median 3.3% and the R edge vanished: the practical case for a later, tighter entry.

criteria.statement: No buy more than 4% above the broken low.
criteria.evidence: The buy point is the broken low. A gap back more than 4% above it is skipped. A later session that opens above the level fills at the open (U 2022-04-05 and INTC 2026-03-31 in the examples). A same-day reclaim fills at the level plus a cent, because the undercut comes after the open: MKSI 2025-11-21 opened 138.24, above the 136.95 level, fell to 134.74 and closed 144.00, so the buy is 136.96 (rescanned 2026-11-10; the first scan filled at the open).

criteria.statement: Never before the reclaim. Buying the undercut itself is guessing.
criteria.evidence: Sperandeo's trigger is the return through the level; Bulkowski: buying the 2B bottom early carries a much greater risk of a failed trade.

criteria.statement: At entry, no more than 10% above the 10-day average.
criteria.evidence: A 2B bottom sits at a low; almost never stretched. The scan applied it.

criteria.statement: A few cents under the lowest low of the undercut (the new extreme). On a same-day reclaim that is the day's low.

measure.value: a few cents under the lowest low from the break to the reclaim

options.basis: under the lowest low of the undercut, the new extreme: Sperandeo (use the new high to compute your initial stop); F62
under the day you buy: the owner's Stop at LOD (QBTS), the same price on a same-day reclaim

criteria.evidence: On a same-day reclaim the two agree. On a 1 to 3 day reclaim the extreme may be an earlier day's low; the dossier asks which (question 6). The scan used 5 cents under the lowest low of the undercut. Turtle Soup Plus One uses the lower of two days' lows.

criteria.statement: If the stop is more than about 3% below the entry, size down so the risk stays inside the grade's budget, or use the tighter entry. Never move the stop closer to make the size bigger.

options.basis: stop under the new low and size down (A5): the dossier's 8.3
skip it (A3)
wait for a tighter spot (the hourly higher low, an inside day) with its own stop: the owner's AMD way

criteria.evidence: The dossier's check: median stop 2.12%, two thirds within 3%; under half within 3% when the reclaim took 1 to 3 days; none when the undercut was over 3%. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim): a stop of 1% of price or less (21,826 hits) reached 3R 67.3% against 42.3% for stops over 2% (was 9,932 hits, 55.5% against 34.7%, with fills at the open), but a sub-1% stop is the one most exposed to slippage and noise. INTC 2026-03-31: a 3.27% stop, just over the line, so half size or the hourly entry. The register's default for all setups is up to one ADR at a lower grade.

criteria.statement: A real stop order with the broker. It only moves up.
criteria.evidence: A4: the stop only moves up. Sperandeo: admit defeat immediately.

criteria.statement: A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if that is past 2R.

measure.what: loss at the first 30-minute low of the gap-down day

criteria.evidence: NVDA 2024-04-19 opened 83.15 and fell to 75.61, a 9% day through the stop with no warning on the daily chart. Bought at the level plus a cent on 04-18 (83.03), the stop was 82.35, 0.82% away.

criteria.statement: Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

measure.what: R at which the stop moves to the entry

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 3R.
criteria.evidence: Among the scan's long winners the median time to 3R was 3 sessions; in the dossier's close-entry check, 6 sessions. Turtle Soup took partial profits in 2 to 6 bars.

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 5R.
If it opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
Trail the last third: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, under the 21-day for a steadier one.
criteria.evidence: JBL 2023-08-18 reached 3R on day 2 and sat at +4% after 20 sessions before the gap to 130: the case for the trims and the trail.

criteria.statement: The first resistance is often the rally high between the two lows; when 3R came, it came in a median of 6 sessions (close entry) or 3 sessions (the level fill).

measure.what: median sessions from the entry to 3R, winners only

criteria.evidence: A note for the lesson, not a rule: the rally high is where the first sellers sit.

criteria.statement: Time stop: still under 1R after 10 trading days, sell.
criteria.evidence: A 2B that has not moved in 10 days has not carried through the other way. Every one of the ten examples was above 1R by the tenth session.

criteria.statement: No close back above the broken low within 3 sessions: it is a breakdown, not a 2B.

measure.what: sessions from the break day without a close back above the prior low

criteria.evidence: The number is the dossier's; the shape is Sperandeo's (a minor 2B fails within one day or less, an intermediate one within three to five days). Five or more closes under the level is a Remount, not a 2B.

criteria.statement: After the entry, a trade under the new low is the exit, at once.
criteria.evidence: Sperandeo: admit defeat immediately and take the loss; you lose properly. TSLA 2023-08-11: the next session gapped under the level and the stock fell four more days to 219.

criteria.statement: After the reclaim, a close back under the broken low within 2 sessions means the failure has failed. A warning: hold to the stop, do not add.

measure.what: sessions after the reclaim in which a close falls back under the broken low

criteria.evidence: The dossier proposed tighten or exit. The owner struck the cut-half rule on 2026-11-09 (my stop is my stop most of the time), and the register's D-136 settles the same question for the U&R (29:8) and the Oops (30:2) as hold to the stop. TSLA 2023-08-11 is the picture: a second, deeper break.

criteria.statement: Below the 50-day with a flat or falling 200-day grades B-, size down or skip; never below the 200-day.

measure.what: reclaim-day close against the 50-day SMA, with the 200-day not higher than 20 sessions ago

criteria.evidence: The owner's 2025-12-07 note said he was adding a variety of short-term undercuts below the MAs to his playbook; question 9 asks whether a 2B below the 50-day but above the 200-day is fine. JBL 2023-08-18 reclaimed under the 50-day and worked.

a_plus: tb.leader: an RS leader (80 or more) in a strong group, above a rising 200-day (tb.ma200_rising)
tb.near_averages: the undercut comes at the 50-day or 200-day
tb.market_washout: the market itself is undercutting and reclaiming its lows; peers in the group do the same (Bracco's chart theme)
tb.level: a clear, obvious prior low many traders can see (a multi-week swing low or last week's low)
tb.depth: a shallow undercut, under about 2%
tb.reclaim_window: a same-day reclaim, closing in the top part of the day's range (tb.reclaim_close)
tb.volume: quiet volume on the break, heavier on the reclaim
tb.clean_lead_in: an orderly drift into the low, no big red news candle before it
b_minus: tb.below_50_grade: below the 50-day with a flat or falling 200-day
tb.depth: a deep undercut (over 3%) bought at the reclaim with the wide stop
tb.volume: a loud break (1.5x volume or more) with a weak reclaim
tb.level: the level is minor (a few days old) or already broken before (tb.first_break)
tb.reclaim_window: the reclaim takes 2 to 3 sessions
tb.leader: a good name but not a top leader; the market still mixed (tb.market_washout)
tb.earnings_window: earnings within days; an obscure or thin name (tb.liquidity)
no_trade: tb.inv_no_reclaim: no close back above the broken low within 3 sessions
tb.never_before_reclaim: the undercut itself, before the reclaim
tb.not_oops: a one-day dip under yesterday's low with no prior swing low
tb.no_chase: more than 4% past the broken low
tb.liquidity: under $10 or under $20 million a day
tb.market_reading: Red; a market still making lower lows with no reclaim (tb.market_washout)

lookalikes.tell: Name the level. A 2B's level is one swing low at least 5 sessions old that price rallied 1 ATR off, on its first break; if the level is a rising 20 EMA or 50-day, a prior high, a round number or the 10-session range low, it is a U&R.

Count the days back to the broken low. An Oops opens under the prior close, breaks yesterday's low and reclaims the prior close the same day; a 2B breaks a swing low at least 5 sessions old and may take up to 3 sessions to close back above it.

Look left for a flat range. A spring's level is the floor of a sideways range of 15 sessions or more, touched at least twice, and the close is back inside the same day or the next; a 2B's level is a single swing low with a rally of at least 1 ATR between it and the break.
Count the closes under the level. A 2B closes back above within 3 sessions; five or more closes under it is a Remount, bought on the retake of the line, not on the reclaim of a low.

Measure the drop into the low. A 2B is a strong stock above its 200-day undercutting a prior low by 3% or less on quiet volume; a capitulation is a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume under the 5, 9 and 20-day with the burst boxes checked, and it may sit under the 200-day as a parabolic long.

invalidations: Before the trigger: no close back above the broken low within 3 sessions, a breakdown (tb.inv_no_reclaim).
Before the trigger: the reclaim day closes in the bottom half of its range (tb.reclaim_close).
Before the trigger: the level was already broken before, or it is only yesterday's low (tb.first_break, tb.not_oops).
Before the trigger: below the 200-day at entry (tb.above_200).
Before the trigger: a report within 3 sessions, wait (tb.earnings_window).
Before the trigger: a market still making lower lows with no reclaim, or an isolated breakdown on news (tb.market_washout, tb.clean_lead_in).
After the entry: a trade under the new low is the exit, at once (tb.after_entry_stop).
After the entry: a close back under the broken low within 2 sessions is the warning that the failure has failed; hold to the stop, do not add (tb.reclaim_fails).
mistakes: Buying the break before the reclaim. Sperandeo's trigger is the return through the level; Bulkowski: a much greater risk.
Holding when the new low breaks. Sperandeo: you lose properly.
Calling any dip under yesterday's low a 2B. The Model Book drawing does this.
Shorting a leader's failed breakout above the 200-day. UCT buys it: the squat.
Taking a deep undercut at full size: the stop is far wider than it looks (HOOD 15.8%, PLTR 11.3%).
Trusting a loud break: heavy volume on the break did worse, as Sperandeo would expect.
2Bs below the 200-day, or in names you would not normally trade.
Expecting the shape alone to pay: it did no better than a random day without the leader, the market low and the entry at the level.
Buying a 2B while the market is still making lower lows (NVDA and AMD, April 2024).

short_mirror.note: The 2B top, dossier 8.6: only below the 200-day (B26, D47). A stock below its 200-day SMA rallies above a prior swing high, fails, and closes back under it within 1 to 3 sessions; short the move back under, stop a few cents above the new high; RS 20 or less, a weak group, not hard to borrow (C31 mirror, D48); the same depth, time, trims and time stop reversed. Not above the 200-day: in a leader a failed breakout is UCT's squat, a buy (buy with 10 toes down). The dossier's check found no edge for 2B-top shorts above the 200-day (22.3% to 3R); the scan's shorts below it reached 3R 39.0% and 5R 26.5% (GLW 2008-08-12, U 2022-04-05). Best in a Red market (D46). Nobody at UCT has written a 2B short on a stock. Whether to teach it is D-001 (28:7).

best_conditions: Long: the indexes are washing out under their own prior lows and reclaiming them (the market put in a low), the reading is turning from Orange or Yellow toward Green, and leaders are undercutting their own lows near the 50-day or 200-day. Start with a few positions (F68). Short: a Red market, a stock below a falling 200-day, a weak bounce into a prior swing high.

management.trail: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.overrides: none. The dossier (8.4) keeps the house defaults and adds a note: the first resistance is often the rally high between the two lows, and 3R came in a median of 3 to 6 sessions. Not ours: Turtle Soup's partial profits in 2 to 6 bars, Sperandeo's exit when prices break past the new 2B high.

base_rate.window: 60 sessions forward, fixed stop 5 cents under the undercut low (the day's low for a same-day reclaim, known only at the close), no trims, no breakeven, no trail, no time stop; 1988-07-12 to 2026-11-09 (bars refreshed after the first scan); the fill at the level plus a cent, or the open when a later session gapped above the level (never the open of the break day); longs above the 200-day, shorts below it
base_rate.rescanned: 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open

was.note: a same-day reclaim was filled at the day's open when it was above the level

same_day_live_stop_check.note: 5-minute bars cannot order events inside one bar

stop_under_1_pct_of_price.note: tight stops pay, when they are real; a sub-1% stop is the most exposed to slippage

close_entry_check_section_4_4.note: entry at the reclaim day's close; geometry alone is not an edge; the scan's higher rate is the fill at the level

failures.why: the April 9 low (83.02) undercut by 0.75% and reclaimed the same day, the 18th (open 84.97, low 82.40, close 84.67, upper half; buy 83.03, stop 82.35, 0.82% away); the next day opened 83.15 and fell to 75.61, a 9% day through the stop with no warning on the daily chart; the market and the chip group were still making lower lows.
the same week, the same group: the February 21 low (161.81) undercut 1.9% on April 15, reclaimed on the 16th (close 163.46), and the next day fell 6% to 154.02, through the stop at 158.71.

the June 26 low (240.70) undercut 1.1% and reclaimed the same day (close 242.65; buy 240.71, stop 237.97, 1.14% away); the next session gapped under the level and the stock fell four more days to 219: a second, deeper break in which the failure had failed.

the 76.93 low (03-02) undercut 0.75% and reclaimed the next day; the open fill 77.98, stop 76.30; the following day reversed from 79.59 to a 76.31 close through the stop, and SPY made a lower low on 04-02.

the 30.82 low (06-12) undercut 1.65% and reclaimed the next day; buy 30.83, stop 30.26; the next day's low touched the stop to the cent and the stock was 31.98 twenty sessions later. Out at once; a retry needs a new trigger.

examples.limits: No RS rating or group (a leader proxy only in the dossier's check, nothing in the scan), no market reading, no earnings filter beyond the ten examples, no clean lead-in test, no trims. Fill at the level plus a cent is the best case for a market order; R is often under 1% of price (23% of long hits have a stop of 0.5% or less), so slippage matters most here. The stop is scored under the undercut's lowest low, which for a same-day reclaim is known only at the close: a 5-minute check of 406 same-day hits gave 60.3% to 3R with that stop and 31.0% with the stop under the low so far at the fill. Survivor universe. Nothing here is a published statistic.

conflicts: Which level: any swing low (Sperandeo); the 20-day low (Turtle Soup); the range low (Wyckoff); any known level (UCT). The card takes a 5-session swing low 5 to 60 sessions old with a 1 ATR rally between, plus the owner's named levels (D-101). The glossary's swing low is 5 sessions each side (28, 33) against 3 in 29 and the app.

How soon: one day for a minor extreme, three to five for an intermediate one, seven to ten for a major one (Sperandeo 1993, 2008); immediately (1994); same day or Plus One (Turtle Soup). The card takes 3 sessions with same or next day graded higher (D-102); the rescan scores the same-day reclaim best (64.3% to 3R, but with a stop known only at the close; 31.0% in the 5-minute live-stop check) against 47.9% next day, and the close-entry check found the same day best.

How deep: Sperandeo gives no number; Bulkowski within 5%; the card takes 3% from A13. Six of UCT's seven named 2Bs went 1.8% to 15.8% under, so UCT's own examples mostly fail the card's depth and teach the deep-undercut problem (D-005).
Volume: Sperandeo's quiet failure against the draft curriculum's heavy volume as the trapped crowd. Both checks lean Sperandeo's way, weakly (D-006).

Entry: a stop order at the level (Sperandeo, Turtle Soup); a market order (E57); the next hourly higher low (the owner's AMD note). The scan's fill at the level gives 56.7% to 3R (was 42.7% when a same-day reclaim was filled at the open; rescanned 2026-11-10); the close entry 27%, the same as a random day; the edge is the fill and the context, not the shape (D-003).

The stop on a slow reclaim: under the lowest low of the undercut (Sperandeo, F62) or under the day you buy (the owner's Stop at LOD). The same price on a same-day reclaim; the dossier's question 6 (D-005).
RS: Bracco's RS names against C31's mean-reversion exemption. The dossier leans to C31; the register's default puts the washout U&R, not the 2B, in the exempt class (D-011).

The short side: every outside source teaches the 2B top as the mirror; UCT buys a leader's failed breakout (the squat) and only reads failed breakouts on the indexes as warnings. The card allows the short only below the 200-day (B26), and whether to teach it is D-001.
The 200-day: about half of liquid 2B bottoms sit below it and did no worse in the check; B26 is a hard rule and wins. GEV (Bracco's name) and the curriculum's SPY 2011 example were below it (D-009).

Chart IQ's two_b_reversal label (computed, as far as traced not shown) fires on bounces under an already-broken low (only 2.5% first breaks, 57.8% never closed back above); it needs the close back above and a first break before anyone surfaces it, and it has no 2B top though the Model Book card says both (D-004).

The Model Book glyph lacks the prior swing low; the coach prompt calls the 2B high-quality with no source; the draft curriculum's partials at 2R and 3R and size-smallest doctrine are not house rules (D-004, D-010).

Scan against the dossier's check: 56.7% to 3R with the fill at the level (was 42.7%, with a same-day fill at the open) against 27.0% with a close entry on a similar rule. The card quotes both and says why they differ.
Near the averages and the clean lead-in are the owner's and Bracco's words without numbers; the card borrows the glossary's touch band and the Oops card's bar-size test and says so.
